statements.quote: A pure text model is blind.
It has never seen a colour, a face, or a curve.
**Multimodal** models remove this handicap: a single network that ingests **images, text, audio, video**, and reasons across them.
The 2024–2025 generation (GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5, InternVL-2, LLaVA-OneVision) is multimodal by default; text-only models are increasingly a special case.
This chapter traces the technical lineage from pixels-as-tensors (see the Computer Vision chapter ) to **pixels-as-tokens** that an LLM can read.
A trained text model lives in a **language embedding space** $\mathbb{R}^d$ where “king” and “queen” sit close together.
statements.section: The Two Towers: Why Aligning Spaces Is Hard

statements.quote: An image encoder (a CNN or Vision Transformer) lives in a **visual embedding space** $\mathbb{R}^{d'}$ where two photographs of the same cat also sit close together.
statements.section: The Two Towers: Why Aligning Spaces Is Hard

statements.quote: The problem: these two spaces are not the same.
statements.section: The Two Towers: Why Aligning Spaces Is Hard

statements.quote: You cannot, in general, do $\vec{v}_\text{cat\,image} - \vec{v}_\text{dog\,image} \approx \vec{v}_\text{“cat”} - \vec{v}_\text{“dog”}$ until they have been aligned.
statements.section: The Two Towers: Why Aligning Spaces Is Hard

statements.quote: The simplest alignment is **contrastive learning**: pull matched (image, caption) pairs together, push mismatched pairs apart.
statements.section: The Two Towers: Why Aligning Spaces Is Hard

statements.quote: This is exactly what **CLIP** does.
statements.section: The Two Towers: Why Aligning Spaces Is Hard

statements.quote: Published by \cite[Radford et al. (OpenAI), 2021]{radford2021clip}, CLIP trains two encoders simultaneously on ~400 million (image, text) pairs scraped from the public web:
* An **image encoder** $f_\theta : \text{Image} \to \mathbb{R}^d$ (originally a ResNet-50, later a ViT-L/14).
* A **text encoder** $g_\phi : \text{Text} \to \mathbb{R}^d$ (a Transformer).
Both are L2-normalized to live on the unit sphere, so cosine similarity equals dot product.

For a batch of $N$ matched pairs, CLIP computes an $N \times N$ similarity matrix and trains both encoders to maximize the diagonal (matched pairs) and minimize the off-diagonal (mismatched pairs) via a **symmetric cross-entropy loss**:
where $\mathbf{I}_i = f_\theta(\text{image}_i)$, $\mathbf{T}_i = g_\phi(\text{text}_i)$, and $\tau$ is a learnable temperature.

After training, CLIP exhibits **zero-shot image classification**: write a prompt like *“a photo of a {label}”* for every candidate class, encode all prompts, encode the image, pick the prompt with highest cosine similarity.
No fine-tuning, no classifier head.
CLIP matched the accuracy of fully-supervised ResNet-50 on ImageNet without ever seeing an ImageNet label.
This is the foundation of every modern vision-language model.
A Vision Transformer (ViT, \cite[Dosovitskiy et al., 2021]{dosovitskiy2021vit}) treats an image as a **sequence of patches**.

statements.quote: The challenge: a pretrained text-only LLM has never seen a pixel.
statements.section: Multimodal LLMs: How a Text Model Learns to See

statements.quote: Three architectural patterns have emerged (often combined):
statements.section: Multimodal LLMs: How a Text Model Learns to See

statements.quote: A pretrained vision encoder (e.g., CLIP-ViT) produces a sequence of visual tokens.
A small **projection MLP** maps each visual token from the vision space into the LLM's text-token embedding space:
The projected visual tokens are concatenated with the text-token sequence and fed to the LLM as if they were ordinary words.
**Only the projection layer is trained initially**; the LLM is frozen.
The visual tokens literally become “foreign-language words” the LLM learns to read.
LLaVA-1.5 (\cite[Liu et al., 2023]{liu2023llava}) used a 7B Vicuna LLM + CLIP-ViT-L/14 + a 2-layer MLP projector.
With ~600k image-instruction pairs, it reached 78.5% on VQAv2, competitive with GPT-4 on several multimodal benchmarks.

The vision tokens are not concatenated into the text sequence; instead, the LLM's self-attention layers are augmented with **cross-attention blocks** that read from the visual sequence at every layer.

Flamingo (\cite[Alayrac et al., 2022]{alayrac2022flamingo}) interleaved gated cross-attention layers between frozen Transformer blocks, training only the cross-attention and a Perceiver Resampler that compressed variable-length image features into a fixed 64-token representation.
The Transformer is trained from scratch on interleaved image, audio, text, and video tokens.
There is no projection layer; the model has always seen pixels as first-class tokens.
Tokens representing 1/24-second audio frames, $16 \times 16$ image patches, and BPE text tokens all flow through the same residual stream.

(The text side is BPE, a **compression** algorithm repurposed as a tokenizer: it fuses frequent patterns into short-ID tokens, so the text enters already in a shorter, lossless form.) This requires vast multimodal training data (trillions of tokens), but produces the most coherent cross-modal reasoning.
Take the prompt *“What is unusual about this image?”* with an attached photo.
statements.section: How a Multimodal LLM Answers a Question

statements.quote: **Encode** the image with the vision tower → sequence of $n$ visual tokens.
statements.section: How a Multimodal LLM Answers a Question

statements.quote: **Project** them into the LLM's token space (or feed via cross-attention).
statements.section: How a Multimodal LLM Answers a Question

statements.quote: **Tokenize** the text prompt as usual.
statements.section: How a Multimodal LLM Answers a Question

statements.quote: **Concatenate**: $\text{[visual tokens] [text tokens]}$.
statements.section: How a Multimodal LLM Answers a Question

statements.quote: **Autoregressive generation** as in any LLM: predict the next text token conditioned on the joint sequence.
statements.section: How a Multimodal LLM Answers a Question

statements.quote: The LLM treats the visual tokens as if they were a foreign language it has been taught to read.
statements.section: How a Multimodal LLM Answers a Question

statements.quote: No new attention mechanism is required, the same Q/K/V machinery already described in the Attention chapter handles the cross-modal mixing, because visual and text tokens occupy the same vector space.
statements.section: How a Multimodal LLM Answers a Question

statements.quote: | Benchmark | What it tests | Why it matters |
| **VQA v2** | Simple visual question answering | The original VQA benchmark; saturated |
| **MMMU** | Multi-discipline college-level multimodal reasoning | Requires expert knowledge + image understanding |
| **MMVet** | Integrated multimodal capabilities | Tests composition of recognition + reasoning + OCR |
| **MathVista** | Mathematical reasoning in visual contexts | Diagrams, plots, geometric figures |
| **DocVQA** | Reading text inside images | Critical for invoices, receipts, forms |
| **MM-Bench** | Broad multimodal evaluation | Now multilingual |
| **RealWorldQA** | Real-world spatial reasoning | Self-driving, robotics |
The leaderboard has shifted dramatically: when MMMU appeared in 2023, text-only models sat near the random baseline.
By 2025, top models (GPT-4o, Claude 3.5, Gemini 1.5 Pro) exceed 70%, and on VQA v2 they exceed 85%.
Multimodal does **not** mean omnipotent:
* **Spatial reasoning**: counting objects (“how many apples?”), understanding left/right relationships, depth ordering, all surprisingly weak.
* **Hallucination amplifies**: an LLM that hallucinates text can hallucinate “the dog is brown” when no dog is present.
* **OCR is brittle**: handwritten text, unusual fonts, or cluttered scenes cause systematic failures.
* **Adversarial fragility**: imperceptible pixel perturbations (see the Security chapter) can flip a model's answer.
* **Resolution wall**: a 1024-token visual sequence compresses 1024×1024 pixels into 1024 vectors.
Mitigations: any-resolution ViTs, “image cropping” at inference, native higher resolutions.
* **Any-to-any models**: GPT-4o, Gemini 2, and others can take image, audio, video *and* produce any of them, generating speech, singing, or video from a text prompt.
* **Video as a long sequence of patches**: video tokens are simply more frames stacked in time.
Gemini 1.5 Pro accepts up to 1 hour of video at native resolution.
* **Embodied multimodal**: robots that fuse camera, lidar, proprioception, and language in one model (RT-2, PaLM-E, OpenVLA).
Multimodal LLMs are conceptually simple:
**Encode** each modality into a sequence of vectors.
**Project** all modalities into a shared token space (or use cross-attention).
**Train** the model as a normal next-token predictor on the joint sequence.

The hard parts are data (curating billions of matched image-text-audio samples, see the Training Data chapter), compute (vision towers + LLMs + alignment data = massive training runs), and evaluation (the benchmarks above are still being developed).
But the architectural recipe is now standard and reproducible, which is why every frontier lab ships multimodal-by-default in 2025.
